questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The history of the Summer Olympic Games
How to take part in dangerous winter sports
Why tennis is not part of the Winter Olympics
Preparations and problems for Beijing 2022
questions.why: They discuss the Beijing Winter Olympics, its controversies and how organisers are preparing.

questions.q: How does Sam describe herself when asked if she's sporty?
options: She plays ice hockey every single weekend
She likes running and watches some TV sport
She never does or watches any sport
She has competed in the Winter Olympics
questions.why: Sam says she likes to go running and might watch some sport on TV.

questions.q: What makes Beijing special as a host city?
options: It's the first to host Summer and Winter Games
It has hosted the Winter Olympics three times
It is the coldest city ever to host the Games
It is the first Asian city to host any Olympics
questions.why: Sam says Beijing will become the first city to have hosted both the Winter and Summer Games.

questions.q: How many events are planned for these Winter Olympics?
options: Seven events in fifteen sports
Fifteen events in seven sports
A record 109 events
Exactly 24 events
questions.why: Neil says a record 109 events over 15 disciplines in seven sports are scheduled.

questions.q: Which problem does Stephen McDonell mention for the organisers?
options: Not enough athletes have agreed to take part
The new stadiums are not yet finished
Tickets have been far too expensive to sell
Covid and claims of human rights abuses
questions.why: He mentions 'coronavirus headaches', 'alleged human rights abuses' and allegations from a tennis star.

questions.q: Why is Covid-19 a 'headache' for the organisers, according to Sam?
options: Many athletes have refused to be vaccinated
It's hard to manage visitors from everywhere
The organisers themselves have been very ill
The events have to be held without any snow
questions.why: She says it makes it difficult to plan, particularly managing people travelling from all parts of the world.

questions.q: Why does a lot of snow have to be made for the Games?
options: The Games are being held in the summer
Real snow is too dangerous for athletes
The area is freezing but mostly dry
The mountains outside Beijing are too low
questions.why: McDonell says the Games will be held in a freezing, mostly dry area, so 'a mountain of snow making is required'.

questions.q: What do athletes think of the conditions?
options: They'll make for fast, high-quality competition
They are too dangerous for the skeleton event
The artificial snow will slow them down
They would prefer to compete in Europe
questions.why: The snow can make for 'quick, dynamic runs', and athletes said the sites will make for high-quality competition.
